name: Cells Arrangement
description: You are given an integer $$$n$$$. You choose $$$n$$$ cells $$$(x_1,y_1), (x_2,y_2),\dots,(x_n,y_n)$$$ in the grid $$$n\times n$$$ where $$$1\le x_i\le n$$$ and $$$1\le y_i\le n$$$. Let $$$\mathcal{H}$$$ be the set of distinct Manhattan distances between any pair of cells. Your task is to maximize the size of $$$\mathcal{H}$$$. Examples of sets and their construction are given in the notes. If there exists more than one solution, you are allowed to output any. Manhattan distance between cells $$$(x_1,y_1)$$$ and $$$(x_2,y_2)$$$ equals $$$|x_1-x_2|+|y_1-y_2|$$$.
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1\le t\le 50$$$) — the number of test cases. Each of the following $$$t$$$ lines contains a single integer $$$n$$$ ($$$2\le n\le 10^3$$$).
output_specification: For each test case, output $$$n$$$ points which maximize the size of $$$\mathcal{H}$$$. It is not necessary to output an empty line at the end of the answer for each test case.
approach_summary: Uncover mathematical invariant or parity constraint. Construct the solution step-by-step maintaining the validity condition without exhaustive search.
